function.name: client_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates of a single client based on the client's name and the status of the mandate. Partners can use this API to retrieve mandate information for their clients. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the client whose mandates are to be fetched.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If not specified, mandates with all statuses are retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches all mandates for all clients associated with a partner, filtered by the status of the mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of mandates to fetch. Possible values are 'active', 'pending', and 'inactive'.

function.name: partner_sips
function.description: Fetch all Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) of all clients associated with a partner, filtered by the given status of the SIP. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the SIPs to be fetched. Valid statuses include 'active', 'stopped', and 'paused'.

message.content:
A **mandate** is a formal, legally binding agreement that authorizes a partner (such as a wealth manager, investment advisor, or financial institution) to act on behalf of a client in managing their investments or executing specific financial transactions. Think of it as a written permission slip that tells the partner what they’re allowed to do—like buying or selling securities, rebalancing portfolios, or making investment decisions—within the scope defined by the client. Key points about mandates: | Feature | What it means | |---------|---------------| | **Legal authority** | Grants the partner the right to make investment decisions or execute trades on the client’s behalf. | | **Scope & limits** | The mandate will specify which assets, strategies, or accounts the partner can manage, and any restrictions (e.g., no high‑risk products). | | **Duration** | Mandates often have a start date and an end date, or they may be ongoing until terminated by either party. | | **Status** | Common statuses include:
• **Active** – the mandate is currently in force.
• **Pending** – awaiting client approval or signature.
• **Inactive** – the mandate has been terminated or expired. | In practice, partners use mandates to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and to maintain transparency with clients. When you see references to “client mandates” or “partner mandates,” it usually refers to retrieving or managing these agreements via APIs or internal systems.
